name: Learn: Network Policies
objective: CKS › Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities. Drill EVERY NetworkPolicy corner harder than the exam: default-deny ingress & egress, allow-by-pod-label, allow-by-namespace, the AND-vs-OR peer trap, port+protocol scoping, ipBlock with except, allow-DNS, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly on the policy spec, per requirement. (kindnet does not enforce policies, so grading is on the authored spec.)
description: Eight strict NetworkPolicy practicals in one namespace. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Default-deny-all ingress
questions.teach:
A **default-deny ingress** policy isolates every pod from inbound traffic. An empty `podSelector: {}` selects all pods in the namespace, and `policyTypes: [Ingress]` with **no** `ingress` rules denies all inbound.

**Gotcha:** list `Ingress` in `policyTypes` but add zero rules — any `ingress` block starts *allowing* traffic instead of denying it.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `netpol-learn`, create a NetworkPolicy `default-deny-ingress` that selects **all** pods and denies all ingress.

Target: empty `podSelector` ({}), `policyTypes: [Ingress]`, and zero ingress rules.
questions.hint: `spec.podSelector: {}`, `policyTypes: [Ingress]`, and omit the `ingress:` key entirely. Apply with `kubectl apply -f -`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-ingress
  namespace: netpol-learn
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
EOF

verification.description: default-deny-ingress: empty podSelector, Ingress type, no ingress rules

questions.title: Allow ingress from a specific pod label
questions.teach:
To let specific source pods in, add an `ingress` rule whose `from` entry is a **`podSelector`** matching their labels. A `from` `podSelector` matches source pods **in the policy's own namespace**.

**Gotcha:** `podSelector: {}` inside `from` means *all pods in this namespace*, but an empty `from: []` matches **no** sources at all.
questions.prompt:
In `netpol-learn`, create a NetworkPolicy `allow-from-client` that selects pods labelled `app=web` and allows ingress **only** from pods labelled `role=client`.

Target: `spec.podSelector` matches `app=web`; one ingress rule with a single `from` entry whose `podSelector` matches `role=client`.
questions.hint: `spec.podSelector.matchLabels.app: web`, then `ingress: [{ from: [{ podSelector: { matchLabels: { role: client } } }] }]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-from-client
  namespace: netpol-learn
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: client
EOF

verification.description: allow-from-client: targets app=web, allows from podSelector role=client

questions.title: Allow ingress from a namespace, on one port
questions.teach:
A `from` entry with a **`namespaceSelector`** admits every pod in any namespace matching that selector. Kubernetes auto-labels each namespace `kubernetes.io/metadata.name=<name>`. Add `ports` to the same rule to restrict which port the traffic may hit.

**Gotcha:** `namespaceSelector` matches namespace **labels**, not the name directly — and `{}` means *all* namespaces.
questions.prompt:
In `netpol-learn`, create a NetworkPolicy `allow-from-monitoring` that selects pods labelled `app=web` and allows ingress from **any** pod in namespace `monitoring`, but **only** on TCP port `80`.

Target: `podSelector` app=web; an ingress rule with a `from` `namespaceSelector` matching `kubernetes.io/metadata.name=monitoring` AND `ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 80}]`.
questions.hint: `from: [{ namespaceSelector: { matchLabels: { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring } } }]` plus `ports: [{ protocol: TCP, port: 80 }]` in the SAME ingress rule.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-from-monitoring
  namespace: netpol-learn
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
EOF

verification.description: allow-from-monitoring: from namespaceSelector name=monitoring, port TCP/80

questions.title: The AND-vs-OR peer trap
questions.teach:
Inside one `from`/`to` list, **separate entries are OR'd**, but `namespaceSelector` and `podSelector` written as **keys of the same entry** are **AND'd** — both must match the source pod. This is the single most-tested NetworkPolicy gotcha.

**Gotcha:** two list items (`- namespaceSelector` then `- podSelector`) means *this namespace OR that pod*; combine them under ONE `- ` to require both.
questions.prompt:
In `netpol-learn`, create a NetworkPolicy `allow-and` selecting pods labelled `app=web`, allowing ingress **only** from pods that are BOTH labelled `role=client` AND live in namespace `monitoring` (one combined peer).

Target: a single ingress `from` entry containing BOTH a `namespaceSelector` (name=monitoring) and a `podSelector` (role=client) — AND semantics, one list item.
questions.hint: ONE `from` list entry with two keys: `- namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring}}` and on the same item `podSelector: {matchLabels: {role: client}}`. Not two separate `- ` items.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-and
  namespace: netpol-learn
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: client
EOF

verification.description: allow-and: ONE from entry with BOTH namespaceSelector(monitoring) AND podSelector(role=client)

questions.title: Default-deny egress + allow DNS
questions.teach:
Egress isolation mirrors ingress: empty `podSelector`, `policyTypes: [Egress]`, and only the egress rules you need. Blocking all egress breaks **DNS**, so you allow port 53 to `kube-system` (CoreDNS) via a `to` `namespaceSelector` plus `ports`.

**Gotcha:** CoreDNS answers on port 53 over **both UDP and TCP** — list both; UDP alone fails on large responses.
questions.prompt:
In `netpol-learn`, create a NetworkPolicy `default-deny-egress-allow-dns` that selects **all** pods, is egress-isolated, and allows egress **only** to port 53 (UDP and TCP) of `kube-system`.

Target: empty `podSelector`, `policyTypes: [Egress]`, one egress rule with a `to` `namespaceSelector` matching `kube-system` and `ports` UDP/53 and TCP/53.
questions.hint: `podSelector: {}`, `policyTypes: [Egress]`, then `egress: [{ to: [{ namespaceSelector: { matchLabels: { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system } } }], ports: [{protocol: UDP, port: 53},{protocol: TCP, port: 53}] }]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-egress-allow-dns
  namespace: netpol-learn
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
EOF

verification.description: default-deny-egress-allow-dns: empty podSelector, Egress, DNS UDP+TCP/53 to kube-system

questions.title: Restrict egress to a specific pod and port
questions.teach:
For least privilege, pin egress to the exact destination a workload needs: a `to` `podSelector` matching the target pods plus the exact `ports`. A `to` `podSelector` alone matches destination pods **in the policy's own namespace**.

**Gotcha:** this policy covers only the DB hop — the pod still needs the separate DNS allow (port 53) or name resolution breaks before it reaches the destination.
questions.prompt:
In `netpol-learn`, create a NetworkPolicy `allow-egress-to-db` that selects pods labelled `app=web` and allows egress **only** to pods labelled `app=db` on **TCP port 5432**.

Target: `podSelector` app=web; `policyTypes: [Egress]`; one egress rule with a `to` `podSelector` matching `app=db` and `ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 5432}]`.
questions.hint: `podSelector.matchLabels.app: web`, `egress: [{ to: [{ podSelector: { matchLabels: { app: db } } }], ports: [{ protocol: TCP, port: 5432 }] }]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-to-db
  namespace: netpol-learn
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: db
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
EOF

verification.description: allow-egress-to-db: app=web → podSelector app=db on TCP/5432

questions.title: Allow ingress from a CIDR, with an exception
questions.teach:
An `ipBlock` peer admits traffic by **CIDR** (for external or node IPs that have no pod labels). `cidr` sets the allowed range and `except` carves out sub-ranges to deny inside it.

**Gotcha:** every entry in `except` must be **within** the `cidr` range, or the API rejects the policy.
questions.prompt:
In `netpol-learn`, create a NetworkPolicy `allow-from-cidr` selecting pods labelled `app=web`, allowing ingress from CIDR `10.0.0.0/16` **except** `10.0.5.0/24`.

Target: `podSelector` app=web; one ingress `from` entry with `ipBlock.cidr=10.0.0.0/16` and `ipBlock.except=[10.0.5.0/24]`.
questions.hint: `from: [{ ipBlock: { cidr: 10.0.0.0/16, except: [10.0.5.0/24] } }]`. The except CIDR must sit inside the main cidr.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-from-cidr
  namespace: netpol-learn
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
        except:
        - 10.0.5.0/24
EOF

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a policy blocking the wrong traffic
questions.teach:
Debugging a NetworkPolicy means reading its spec: check `podSelector` (who it applies to), `policyTypes`, and the exact `from`/`to`/`ports`. A one-field mistake — wrong label, wrong port, wrong selector kind — silently blocks the traffic you meant to allow.

**Gotcha:** fix the existing policy's spec in place; a second overlapping policy only adds more allowed paths, it can't *remove* another policy's restriction.
questions.prompt:
Policy `allow-api` in `netpol-learn` is meant to let pods labelled `app=web` receive ingress from pods labelled `role=client` on **TCP port 8080**, but it's misconfigured and blocks that traffic. Diagnose and fix it in place — do not rename or recreate from scratch.

Target end-state: `allow-api` selects `app=web`, `policyTypes: [Ingress]`, one ingress rule from `podSelector` `role=client` on `ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 8080}]`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n netpol-learn get netpol allow-api -o yaml` and compare each field to the target: the ingress `from` podSelector and/or the port are wrong. Edit it: `kubectl -n netpol-learn edit netpol allow-api`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-api
  namespace: netpol-learn
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: client
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
EOF

verification.description: allow-api fixed: app=web ← podSelector role=client on TCP/8080
